headline: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES ‘SEVA SAMMAN PARV’ AND ‘YUVA PRABODHAN’ ON THE OCCASION OF NUAKHAI FESTIVAL IN RAIPUR
subhead: IT IS OUR COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY TO RESPECT FOOD, ACKNOWLEDGE THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF OUR FARMERS, AND PROTECT OUR NATURAL RESOURCES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
paras: The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced ‘Seva Samman Parv’ and ‘Yuva Prabodhan’ on the occasion of the Nuakhai festival in Raipur, Chhattisgarh today (October 22, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Nuakhai Milan Samaroh is not merely a cultural celebration; it is a tribute to our rich traditions, social harmony and unity. Such occasions provide us with an opportunity to reconnect with our roots, take pride in our cultural heritage, and pass on the life values to future generations.

The President stated that the Nuakhai festival is a celebration of our agricultural traditions, an expression of gratitude toward nature and a testament to the spirit of community. This festival reminds us that food is not just a means to satisfy hunger; it is a symbol of the hard work of our farmers, the generosity of Mother Earth and the invaluable gifts of nature. She underlined that it is our collective responsibility to respect food, acknowledge the contributions of our farmers, and protect our natural resources.

Addressing the youth present in large numbers, the President said that circumstances may vary, and challenges may differ; yet, youth should possess a deep-seated drive to innovate, to create something better, and to establish their own unique identity. She said that when they align their individual endeavours with collective and national goals, they pave the way for the nation’s progress. She advised them to dream big, broaden their horizons, uphold the highest standards of conduct, and place service to society and the nation at the centre of their endeavours. She encouraged the youth to pursue every endeavour with honesty, integrity and sensitivity. She emphasised that nation-building is not accomplished through major decisions alone, but also through the small, sincere efforts of millions of citizens. She urged them to combine knowledge with humility, ambition with ethical values, and success with a spirit of service, highlighting that these qualities would strengthen their contribution to the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

The President was happy to note the participation of a large number of women in the Nuakhai Milan Samaroh. She said that the nation is moving forward with the goal of a Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. To achieve this goal, the equal participation of women is absolutely essential. She urged all women to participate actively in the affairs of the nation and society. She said that when they progress, the benefits will extend not only to them or their family but to the entire society and the nation. She urged men, especially the youth, to provide an environment for their sisters and daughters in which they can realize their dreams without any barriers. She said that respect for women should not merely be expressed in words; it must be reflected in their behaviour, mindset, and daily conduct.

The President was happy to note that through the efforts of the central and state governments, combined with their own strength of will, the youth of Chhattisgarh have moved away from the path of Naxalism and joined the mainstream. The light of development is now replacing the darkness of terror. She said that this transformation is leading to the well-being of the young people and their families while accelerating the development of the state and the country.

headline: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Inaugurates Conference on Cooperative Federalism and Law Reforms in New Delhi
subhead: “Legal Reforms Must Keep Pace with Changing Times”: Vice-President Urges States to Repeal Obsolete Laws for Efficient Governance “The Ultimate Purpose of Law Is to Ensure a Just, Secure and Dignified Life for Every Citizen”: Vice-President “Strong States Contribute to a Strong Union; Cooperative Governance Transforms Constitutional Ideals into Public Good”: Vice-President
paras: The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspective’, organised by the Law Commission of India at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the conference on ‘Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms: National and State Perspectives’ in New Delhi today. Emphasising the spirit of ‘Team India’, he called for greater consultation, coordination and shared responsibility between the Centre and States, noting that political differences must never come in the way of the larger public interest.

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that India’s greatest strength lies in its unity in diversity, with the Constitution providing the framework to balance the strength of the Union with the responsibilities and legitimate autonomy of the States. He emphasised that the true strength of Indian federalism lies in respecting diversity while working towards common national objectives.

Highlighting the importance of cooperative and competitive federalism, the Vice-President said that the vision of ‘Team India’, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, calls for consultation, coordination and shared responsibility between the Centre and the States. He noted that political differences should never come in the way of working together for the larger public interest.

Emphasising the importance of legal reforms in achieving Viksit Bharat @2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that development must be supported by sound laws, transparent institutions, efficient administration and justice for all.

The Vice-President highlighted the replacement of three colonial-era criminal laws and the repeal of over 1,700 obsolete laws in the last twelve years as major steps towards modernising India’s legal framework. He urged State Law Commissions to identify and recommend the amendment or repeal of outdated laws to promote ease of living and efficient governance.

Stressing that cooperative federalism in law reforms does not imply uniformity in every matter, the Vice-President said that the Union and States must work together where their constitutional responsibilities converge, while preserving the States’ legitimate space to address their specific needs. He called for stronger coordination among the Law Commission of India, State Law Commissions and State Law Departments through inter-State consultations, sharing of best practices and systematic review of outdated laws.

Referring to the Sengol installed in Parliament as a symbol of righteous authority and ethical governance, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan invoked the timeless wisdom of Tamil saint-poet Thiruvalluvar on good governance and adherence to the rule of law. He emphasised that good governance, rather than the exercise of power alone, is the foundation of lasting success and prosperity.
The Vice-President expressed hope that the conference would produce concrete and actionable recommendations towards a coherent, responsive and citizen-centric legal framework.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Chairperson of the Law Commission of India, Justice Dinesh Maheshwari; Member Secretary, Law Commission of India, Dr. Anju Rathi Rana; and Member of the Law Commission of India, Prof. D. P. Verma, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion.
PR/ASM/VMJ

headline: Prime Minister receives a telephone call from Prime Minister Netanyahu
subhead: Both leaders reaffirm their commitment to further strengthening the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership The two leaders discuss developments in West Asia and emphasise the urgent need to restore peace and stability PM Modi reiterated India’s call for dialogue and diplomacy
paras: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi received a telephone call today from the Prime Minister of Israel, H.E. Mr. Benjamin Netanyahu.
The two leaders welcomed the sustained momentum in India-Israel relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the Special Strategic Partnership between the two countries.
The leaders also exchanged views on recent developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region.
Prime Minister Modi reiterated India’s call for dialogue and diplomacy as the way forward.
The two leaders agreed to remain in touch.

headline: PM to Inaugurate Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on 23 October
subhead: Programme marks culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission
paras: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at 11 AM on 23 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The three-day Sammelan, being held from 23 to 25 October 2026, will bring together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.

The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita, produced by Chinmaya Mission with music by Ilaiyaraaja, at Gangaikonda Cholapuram in Tamil Nadu. Several initiatives and events were organised during the year, including mass havans at multiple locations, consecration of the Maa Soundarya Chinmayi Temple in Tripura, and Chinmaya Gita Samarpanam under which over 1 lakh people across the world chanted the 15th chapter of the Bhagavad Gita together online. A major initiative of the celebrations was Gita Panchamrit, centred on five select verses of the Bhagavad Gita. To take the message of the Gita across the country, 15 young members of Chinmaya Yuva Kendra undertook the Chinmaya Amrit Yatra, travelling over 40,000 km across the country.

headline: India-Poland Joint Statement
paras: At the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Poland, H.E. Mr. Donald Tusk, paid an official visit to India from 21-23 October 2026. Prime Minister Tusk was accompanied by a high-level delegation, including around 100 leading CEOs and industry representatives.
Prime Minister Modi and Prime Minister Tusk held comprehensive discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues of mutual interest.

The Prime Ministers recalled Prime Minister Modi’s landmark visit to Poland in August 2024, when the bilateral relationship was elevated to a Strategic Partnership and the India-Poland Action Plan for 2024-2028 was adopted. They endorsed the mid-term review of the Action Plan done by the Indian External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and the Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski in Warsaw in September 2026.

The Prime Ministers noted that the present visit imparts fresh momentum to the Strategic Partnership and reaffirmed their determination to translate this partnership into concrete, time-bound and mutually beneficial outcomes.

The Leaders agreed to intensify high-level political exchanges and institutional dialogue, and encouraged closer engagement between their Parliaments, state and regional authorities, think tanks and policy institutions.

The Prime Ministers underlined the importance of the historic India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026 in New Delhi, the Towards 2030: A Joint India-European Union Comprehensive Strategic Agenda, the conclusion of the EU-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the Comprehensive Framework of Cooperation on Mobility. On the FTA, they called for its early signing and ratification as well as timely implementation, with a view to unlocking new opportunities for trade and investment, diversifying and strengthening critical value chains, and opening new markets.
Trade, Economic Cooperation and Investment

Prime Minister of India congratulated Poland on crossing the USD 1 trillion GDP mark and noted the resilience and dynamism of the Polish economy. Poland appreciated India’s record as the fastest growing big economy and its impressive trajectory to become a USD 10 trillion economy in the coming years. The Leaders recognised the complementary strengths of the two economies and the opportunities arising from India’s and Poland’s respective growth paths.

The Leaders set the target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030. Prime Minister of India invited Polish companies to expand their investments and operations in India and to benefit from India’s large market, skilled workforce and growing manufacturing and innovation ecosystem. Prime Minister Tusk appreciated Indian investment in Poland and highlighted Poland’s strength as a gateway for Indian businesses seeking to expand their presence in Central and Eastern Europe and the wider European market.
Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in agriculture by resuming the activities of the bilateral working group, aimed at intensifying bilateral trade and cooperation.

The Leaders welcomed the India-Poland Business Forum held during the visit with the presence of leading CEOs and industry representatives from both countries. They encouraged businesses to explore partnerships in sectors including industrial machinery, defence, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, mining and critical minerals, energy, ICT and other areas of mutual interest.

The Leaders underscored the importance of resilient and diversified supply chains, promotion of medium and small enterprises, innovation-led growth and digital transformation. They recognised the transformative role of digital technologies and artificial intelligence in economic growth, productivity and public service delivery. Acknowledging the India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda, both leaders also agreed to undertake collaborative research on AI, semiconductors and Quantum technologies as well as to enhance Startup partnerships. They agreed to encourage closer cooperation between enterprises, research institutions and innovation ecosystems in both countries.
Defence and Security Cooperation

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening defence and security cooperation. They welcomed the outcomes of the 8th meeting of the Joint Working Group on Defence, held in Warsaw in September 2026, and agreed to maintain regular exchanges between the defence establishments of both countries.

The Leaders welcomed growing interaction between Indian and Polish defence industries and encouraged them to identify commercially viable areas of cooperation. A Defence Industry Dialogue was proposed by the leaders to encourage the development of a forward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperation, including greater business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of industrial collaboration.

Both leaders welcomed the signing of the India-EU Security and Defence Partnership in January 2026 and underlined the importance of strengthening India-Poland cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, cybersecurity and defence innovation, including through business and other platforms, contributing to enhanced technological resilience and closer India-EU security and defence cooperation.
Both sides underlined the importance of having an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressed their expectation that it would be signed soon.
Space Cooperation / New technologies

The Leaders recognised cooperation in the space sector as a key element of the Strategic Partnership and encouraged stronger institutional and industry-level engagement, welcoming efforts to identify concrete areas of mutually beneficial cooperation.
Both Leaders highlighted opportunities of close cooperation on semiconductors.
The Prime Ministers emphasised the potential for collaboration in circular economy and recovery industry, particularly focusing on recycling of batteries and refining of rare earth minerals.
They underlined opportunities for closer cooperation in geology, mining and critical minerals sector. An MoU in this regard is under negotiation.
Connectivity, maritime and shipping

The Leaders welcomed the prospect of exploring the opportunities for enhancing direct flights on the routes between Poland and India. They encouraged the civil aviation/ aeronautical authorities to hold direct talks as a symbol of strengthening bilateral relations.
Both sides highlighted the prospect of cooperation in the shipping industry as well as in maritime security.

The Leaders recognised the importance of cooperation between ports in advancing a secure, resilient, and integrated network that diversifies global supply chains, shortens transit times, and safeguards critical infrastructure against geopolitical disruptions. The two leaders noted the importance of improving connectivity, including through the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) initiative.
The Prime Ministers agreed on developing scientific cooperation in polar affairs.
Science, Education and Academic Cooperation

The Leaders noted Poland’s long tradition of scholarship in Indology and Sanskrit and welcomed the ICCR Chair of Indian Studies at the Jagiellonian University in Kraków. They acknowledged the presence of Polish language teachers at Indian universities. They also noted the extensive network of cooperation between Indian and Polish higher education institutions and encouraged deeper institutional partnerships, student and faculty exchanges, and called for more collaborative research.
Culture and People-to-People Ties

The Leaders reaffirmed that strong people-to-people ties are an important pillar of the Strategic Partnership. They welcomed growing exchanges between the two peoples, including among professionals and tourists and agreed to encourage cultural cooperation, including sports, youth exchanges and tourism. An agreement on cooperation in the fields of culture, science and higher education will be concluded soon. A Cooperation agreement between the National Archives of India and General Director of the State Archives of the Republic of Poland was concluded and would be signed soon.

Both sides acknowledged that the memorial of the Maharaja Jamsaheb (popularly known as the Good Maharaja in Poland) and the Principality of Kolhapur in Warsaw represent a living bridge between the people of the two friendly countries and an evocative chapter of history, where India provided a home to thousands of Polish women and children during World War-II. Both sides expressed satisfaction that two editions of the Jam Saheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme had taken place, including most recently in October 2026.
Both sides recalled with appreciation the assistance provided by the Polish authorities to more than 2,000 Indian students stranded in Ukraine under Operation Ganga.
Multilateral Cooperation and Global Issues

The Leaders underlined the importance of multilateralism with the UN Charter at its core. Both sides agreed that the United Nations needs structural reforms, including through the expansion of the UN Security Council in both permanent and non-permanent categories in order to stay relevant, credible and effective. The Polish side expressed its support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as reiterated its support for India’s candidature for a non-permanent seat in the UNSC for 2028-29.

The Leaders highlighted the role of the G20 as a key forum for international cooperation. They expressed their readiness to cooperate in the G20 tracks and workstreams in which the Republic of Poland participates or may be invited to participate.

The two leaders expressed their deepest concern over the war raging in Ukraine, including its terrible and tragic humanitarian consequences. They reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity. They also noted the negative impacts of the war in Ukraine with regard to global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.

The two leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism leading to terrorism in all their forms and manifestations, irrespective of their motivations, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there can be no justification for terrorism on any grounds. They condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee. Both sides also called upon all countries to continue to work towards eliminating terrorist safe havens and infrastructure as well as to disrupt terrorism financing networks. Both leaders called for the early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT) at the United Nations. They agreed to have a dialogue on counter-terrorism.

The Leaders reaffirmed the importance of a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific and of respect for international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). They underscored the importance of freedom of navigation and the peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law. India invited Poland to join the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI).

Both Leaders welcomed the first Foreign Ministers' Meetings of India and the Visegrad Group (V4), comprising Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic. They reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen cooperation through the V4+India format and to build a forward-looking partnership based on shared interests and complementarities.

The Leaders underscored the need for accelerated global action on climate change, and reaffirmed their support for the UNFCCC process and the Paris Agreement. They recognised the growing risks posed by extreme weather events, environmental degradation and biodiversity loss and encouraged closer bilateral cooperation in clean energy, sustainable technologies and climate-resilient development. They highlighted the need to increase the share of home-grown clean energy in national energy mixes to enhance energy security, protect the climate, and improve industrial competitiveness. India welcomed Poland’s announcement of joining the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI). India invited Poland to join the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance.

Prime Minister Tusk thanked Prime Minister Modi for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation. The Leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment to further deepen and diversify the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and to ensure effective implementation of the Action Plan (2024-2028) through regular high-level engagement and strengthened institutional cooperation.
Prime Minister Tusk also extended an invitation to Prime Minister Modi to visit Poland.

headline: Prime Minister’s Press Statement during Joint Press Statement with the Prime Minister of Poland
paras: Your Excellency, Mr. Prime Minister
दोनों देशों के delegates,
मीडिया के साथियों,
नमस्कार!
पोलैंड के प्रधानमंत्री जी का भारत में हार्दिक स्वागत करते हुए मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है।
2024 में मेरी पोलैंड यात्रा के दौरान उन्होंने मेरा और मेरे डेलिगेशन का आत्मीय स्वागत किया था। उस यात्रा में हमने अपने संबंधों को Strategic Partnership का दर्जा दिया।

इसी मजबूत आधार पर, पिछले दो वर्षों में हमारी साझेदारी ने नई गति पकड़ी है। और आज प्रधानमंत्री जी के साथ हुई बैठक में, हमने अपनी Strategic Partnership को और सुदृढ़ करने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए हैं।
Friends,
भारत और पोलैंड की मित्रता केवल कूटनीतिक संबंधों पर नहीं, बल्कि मानवता और संवेदना की साझी विरासत पर आधारित है।

द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान जामनगर और कोल्हापुर के राजपरिवारों ने, पोलैंड के हजारों बच्चों और परिवारों को भारत में आश्रय दिया था। आज भी पोलैंड के लोग जाम साहब को बड़े सम्मान से “दोब्री महाराजा”, यानी “Good Maharaja” के नाम से याद करते हैं।

2022 में यूक्रेन से हमारे स्टूडेंट्स की सुरक्षित वापसी में सहयोग देकर, पोलैंड ने भी मानवता की इसी भावना को आगे बढ़ाया। मुझे खुशी है कि जाम साहब यूथ एक्सचेंज प्रोग्राम के माध्यम से, पोलैंड के युवा भारत आ रहे हैं और हमारी ऐतिहासिक मित्रता को नई पीढ़ी तक ले जा रहे हैं।
Friends,
आज विश्व अनिश्चितता और बदलाव के दौर से गुजर रहा है। ऐसे समय में भी भारत और पोलैंड, दोनों ही ग्रोथ, टेक्नॉलजी और इनोवेशन के महत्वपूर्ण केंद्र के रूप में उभर रहे हैं।
पिछले वर्ष पोलैंड की GDP ने एक ट्रिलियन डॉलर का ऐतिहासिक पड़ाव पार किया। इसके लिए मैं प्रधानमंत्री जी को बहुत बहुत बधाई देता हूँ। वहीं, भारत ने भी पिछले क्वार्टर में 7.8% की शानदार ग्रोथ दर्ज की है।

हमारी बढ़ती आर्थिक ताकत ने भारत-पोलैंड साझेदारी के लिए नए अवसर पैदा किए हैं। और भारत-यूरोपियन यूनियन Free Trade Agreement ने इन अवसरों को और व्यापक बनाया है। इस समझौते के लागू होने पर भारत से पोलैंड को, मशीनरी, केमिकल्स, प्लास्टिक्स और इंजीनियरिंग गुड्स के निर्यात के नए अवसर खुलेंगे। साथ-ही, रेलवे और मोबिलिटी, एडवांस्ड मैन्युफैक्चरिंग, फूड प्रोसेसिंग और बायो-टेक जैसे क्षेत्रों में हम पोलैंड से नए निवेश आकर्षित करेंगे।

मुझे विशेष खुशी है कि प्रधानमंत्री जी एक बड़े बिज़नेस डेलिगेशन के साथ भारत आए हैं। हमें विश्वास है कि दोनों देशों की कंपनियाँ मिलकर विश्व के लिए trusted supply chains विकसित करेंगी, और 2030 तक द्विपक्षीय व्यापार को दोगुना करने के हमारे साझा लक्ष्य को भी साकार करेंगी।
Friends,

आज हमने डिफेन्स, स्पेस और न्यूक्लियर एनर्जी में संबंधों को प्रगाढ़ करने पर सहमति बनाई है। इन सभी स्ट्रैटीजिक क्षेत्रों में हम पोलैंड की कम्पनीज़ को भारत के साथ co-development और co-production करने के लिए आमंत्रित करते हैं।
क्रिटिकल मिनरल्स और कोल गैसिफिकेशन में भी, हम पोलैंड की एक्स्पर्टीज़ को साथ लेकर नई साझेदारियाँ विकसित करेंगे।
IT और साइबर सिक्योरिटी में हमारे संबंध पहले से ही मजबूत हैं। कई भारतीय IT कम्पनीज़ पोलैंड में काम कर रही हैं।इस सहयोग को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, हमने भारत-पोलैंड start-up bridge स्थापित करने पर सहमति बनाई है।

हम दोनों देशों के युवाओं के बीच टेक्नॉलजी hackathons भी आयोजित करेंगे। इन पहलों से AI, साइबर, फिन-टेक और अन्य emerging technologies में हमारे सहयोग को नई गति मिलेगी, और दोनों देशों के युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर पैदा होंगे।
Friends,
कल्चरल और People-to-people ties हमारे संबंधों की सबसे बड़ी ताकत हैं। हमें बहुत खुशी है कि पोलैंड में संस्कृत अध्ययन और Indology की समृद्ध परंपरा है।
क्राकोव शहर में हमने Indian Studies Chair की स्थापना की है। आज हमने कल्चर और एजुकेशन, और साथ-साथ स्पोर्ट्स और टुरिज़म में भी सहयोग को और सुदृढ़ करने का निर्णय लिया है।
Friends,

आज हमने regional और global developments पर भी विस्तार से चर्चा की। भारत और पोलैंड, दोनों डेमॉक्रैटिक वैल्यूस और rule of law में विश्वास रखते हैं। हमारा मानना है कि global governance institutions को अधिक सशक्त और प्रभावी बनाने के लिए रिफॉर्म आवश्यक है।
यूक्रेन हो या पश्चिमी एशिया, भारत शांति की दिशा में किये गए हर सार्थक प्रयास का समर्थन करता रहेगा।
Your Excellency,
हमारे साझा इतिहास में मानवता और संवेदना की गहरी छाप है। और हमारे साझा भविष्य में इनोवेशन और टेक्नॉलजी सहयोग की असीम संभावनाएँ हैं।
मुझे विश्वास है कि आपकी इस यात्रा से, भारत-पोलैंड Strategic Partnership को नई ऊर्जा और नई ऊँचाई मिलेगी। एक बार फिर, आपका और आपके डेलिगेशन का हार्दिक स्वागत है।
आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

headline: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting the importance of humility and continuous learning
paras: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, highlighting the importance of remaining humble over limited success and the constant need to learn and grow.
The Prime Minister wrote on X;
"खद्योतो द्योतते तावद् यावन्नोदयते शशी।
उदिते तु सहस्रांशौ न खद्योतो न चन्द्रमाः।।"

A firefly appears to shine only in the absence of the moon. But when the sun rises, neither the firefly's glow nor the moon can be seen. Likewise, the significance of a lesser achievement lasts only until something greater comes along. Therefore, one should remain humble rather than become arrogant over limited success and continue to learn and grow.
खद्योतो द्योतते तावद् यावन्नोदयते शशी। उदिते तु सहस्रांशौ न खद्योतो न चन्द्रमाः।। https://t.co/86NrPIbyXO

headline: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to be Held in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on 26–27 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker
subhead: The Prime Minister of India will grace the forum and meet the leaders of visiting delegations: Lok Sabha Speaker Presiding Officers of Parliaments, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries from BRICS member and partner countries to deliberate on strategic priorities for parliaments: Lok Sabha Speaker Global parliamentary leaders to assemble in New Delhi for the conference being hosted under India's chairship on the theme of people-centric development: Lok Sabha Speaker Deliberations to cover parliamentary functioning in relation to institutional resilience, ethical AI and digital transformation, global governance reforms and sustainable development: Lok Sabha Speaker International Affairs Committees of BRICS member and partner countries to discuss parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices: Lok Sabha Speaker
paras: The Parliament of India will host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on 26 and 27 October 2026 in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. The conference will be inaugurated on 26 October.

Addressing a press conference at Parliament House today, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla said that the conference marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy. It will bring together Presiding Officers and parliamentary leaders from BRICS member and partner countries, Union Ministers, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh, Presiding Officers of State Legislatures, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries.
The Lok Sabha Speaker stated that the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi would grace the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations.

He further stated that the conference would feature bilateral and multilateral interactions with the leaders of visiting delegations and parliamentary friendship groups. A meeting of the Secretaries of the delegations will be held on 25 October 2026 to finalise the Joint Statement of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
Highlighting the central theme of the programme, he said that the Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development.”
He added that, building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would facilitate consensus-based dialogue through the following four high-level sessions:
(i) Resilience: The critical role of parliaments in strengthening institutions to ensure a better future.
(ii) Innovation: Promoting human-centred innovation in artificial intelligence and digital technologies through parliaments.
(iii) Cooperation: Ensuring a more representative system of global governance through parliamentary cooperation.
(iv) Sustainability: The role of parliaments in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for our countries.

In addition, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of the parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices.

Shri Birla further stated that, alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme. The Vice-President of India will host a banquet in honour of the distinguished guests.
Members of the delegations will visit the Parliament of India and also enjoy cultural visits in Delhi. The conference will conclude on 27 October.

भारत की संसद द्वारा 26 और 27 अक्टूबर 2026 को आयोजित होने जा रहे 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum से पूर्व आज संसद परिसर, नई दिल्ली में प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस को संबोधित किया। इस ऐतिहासिक सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स के 11 Member Countries तथा 10 Partner Countries की संसदों के पीठासीन अधिकारी और संसदीय शिष्टमंडल भाग लेंगे। इस अवसर पर माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी की गरिमामयी उपस्थिति रहेगी। प्रधानमंत्री जी कार्यक्रम में सहभागिता करेंगे तथा आगंतुक अतिथियों के साथ संवाद करेंगे। 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम का मुख्य विषय “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development” है। इसके अंतर्गत Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability जैसे महत्वपूर्ण विषयों पर विचार-विमर्श होगा। सम्मेलन में ब्रिक्स सदस्य एवं भागीदार देशों की अंतरराष्ट्रीय मामलों संबंधी संसदीय समितियों के अध्यक्षों की विशेष बैठक, द्विपक्षीय एवं बहुपक्षीय संवाद तथा विभिन्न देशों के साथ गठित Parliamentary Friendship Groups की बैठकें भी आयोजित की जाएँगी। माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में सितंबर 2026 में आयोजित ब्रिक्स शिखर सम्मेलन सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न हुआ, जिसमें सभी सदस्य देशों ने भाग लिया और महत्वपूर्ण घोषणाएँ की गईं। 12वाँ ब्रिक्स संसदीय फोरम इसी दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है, जो विभिन्न देशों के बीच संसदीय सहयोग को सुदृढ़ करने और साझा वैश्विक चुनौतियों के समाधान हेतु संवाद को आगे बढ़ाएगा। मुझे विश्वास है कि यह सम्मेलन लोकतांत्रिक परंपराओं को सशक्त करने, जनता के प्रति जवाबदेही बढ़ाने, संवाद के माध्यम से सहमति बनाने, संसदीय संस्थाओं में तकनीक के उपयोग को बढ़ावा देने तथा वैश्विक चुनौतियों के समाधान में संसदीय सहयोग को नई ऊँचाइयों तक ले जाने का मार्ग प्रशस्त करेगा। #BRICS2026 #BRICSParliamentaryForum

headline: Secretary DARE Calls for Reimagining Agricultural Higher Education Through Global Partnerships
subhead: Addressing Indian agricultural diaspora at the World Food Prize Foundation programme in the United States virtually, Dr Jat highlights industry–academia collaboration, policy dialogue and international knowledge exchange
paras: Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), has called for reimagining agricultural higher education to prepare future professionals to address global challenges, including climate change, natural resource degradation, biodiversity loss and the growing demand for nutritious and healthy food.

Addressing a Roundtable organized on the sidelines of the '2026 Norman E Borlaug International Dialogue' during the World Food Prize Foundation at Des Moines in the United States virtually, Dr. Jat delivered his remarks as President of the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS), India. He acknowledged the Academy’s representation at the programme by its Secretary, Dr. B.S. Dwivedi; Foreign Secretary, Dr. Karim Meredia; and Convener of the International Chapter for the Western Hemisphere, Dr. P.V. Varaprasad.

In his address, Dr Jat emphasised the need to transform agricultural education and research to meet the evolving requirements of agri-food systems. He highlighted India’s long-standing partnerships with global institutions, noting that international collaboration enables mutual learning and provides opportunities to share scientific and educational advancements.

He stressed the importance of moving beyond production-centric agriculture towards an integrated agri-food systems and value-chain approach. He underscored the need for stronger collaboration between academia and industry to develop industry-ready human resources and facilitate industry participation across the agri-food value chain, including support for farmers.

Highlighting the role of NAAS in agricultural policy and research, Dr Jat noted the importance of policy dialogues, policy papers and policy briefs in addressing critical issues in agricultural research and development. He emphasised the need to bring together researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, industry and other stakeholders to develop collaborative solutions to emerging challenges.

Dr Jat also highlighted efforts to connect the Indian agricultural diaspora with domestic research and educational institutions. Strengthening these networks, he noted, can facilitate international knowledge exchange and contribute to reimagining agricultural higher education through global expertise and experience.

Referring to efforts to expand international institutional partnerships, Dr Jat highlighted the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Council for Agricultural Science and Technology (CAST). The partnership is expected to create new avenues for cooperation in agricultural research, capacity development and knowledge exchange.

Dr. Jat expressed confidence that stronger international partnerships would contribute to advancing agricultural research, education and extension, with particular relevance for countries of the Global South. He called for collective efforts to transform agri-food systems and build a more resilient and sustainable future for agriculture worldwide.

headline: India Post Creates History, Crosses ₹4,000 Crore Revenue Mark for Two Consecutive Quarters
subhead: Department records 24% revenue growth in H1 FY 2026-27, reaching ₹8,212.7 crore; Parcels register 71% growth. Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia emphasises customer centricity, business diversification, innovation and digitisation to sustain India Post’s growth momentum.
paras: The Department of Posts has achieved a historic milestone by crossing the ₹4,000 crore quarterly revenue mark for two consecutive quarters for the first time. The Department recorded revenue of ₹8,212.7 crore during the first half of FY 2026-27 (April-September 2026), registering a year-on-year growth of 24% over ₹6,636 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

(L–R) Ms. Manisha Sinha, DGPS; Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union MoS for Communications and Rural Development; Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; and Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), during the Q2 Review Meeting in
New Delhi.

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region chaired the Second Quarter (Q2) Review at New Delhi, today. Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), Members of the Postal Services Board, Chief Postmasters General of all Postal Circles and senior officers of the Directorate attended the meeting.
The Department earned ₹4,201.5 crore in Q2 (Jul-September 2026), registering year-on-year growth of 25% and an increase of 5% over Q1.
Growth Across Business Verticals

All six business verticals recorded year-on-year growth. PLI/RPLI grew by 44%, Mails by 36%, Post Office Savings Bank (POSB) by 18%, International Relations & Global Business by 38%, and Parcels by 71%.

The Parcels vertical generated ₹318.9 crore in Q2, with Kerala, North East, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar exceeding their quarterly targets. Mails revenue increased by 26% over Q1, with 12 Postal Circles achieving or exceeding their Q2 targets. POSB contributed ₹1,987 crore, while PLI/RPLI achieved 92% of its quarterly target.
Postal Circle Performance and Efficiency

Seven Postal Circles achieved 90% or more of their proportionate Q2 targets. Bihar led with 97.15%, followed by West Bengal at 97.07% and North East at 94.79%. For H1, West Bengal recorded 95.72% achievement, followed by Bihar at 95.12% and Andhra Pradesh at 94.63%.

Eighteen of the 23 Postal Circles improved their target achievement over Q1. The Expenditure Cost Ratio reached 42% including pension expenditure and 62% excluding pension expenditure. Twenty-two Circles improved their ratios over Q1.
Recognition of Outstanding Postal Circles

In recognition of their performance during the first quarter(April–June 2026), Andhra Pradesh Postal Circle was awarded and Bihar Postal Circle was awarded for the second quarter(July–September 2026), for their achievement against their respective proportionate business targets. Bihar Circle achieved 97.15%, followed closely by West Bengal Circle at 97.07% and North East Circle at 94.79%. Their performance reflects focused business efforts and progress towards the Department’s revenue objectives. The recognition also underscores the importance of sustained performance, effective business planning and continued efforts to strengthen revenue generation across Postal Circles.
Ministers Emphasise on Sustainable Growth

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region congratulated officers and employees on the achievement and emphasised the need to sustain growth through customer acquisition, service excellence and customer retention. He called for greater business diversification, stronger leadership, innovation and a customer-centric approach, including flexible pricing for bulk customers, subject to applicable policies and approvals. He also emphasised the need to accelerate the digitalisation of services offered by India Post to enhance customer experience, improve operational efficiency and strengthen the Department’s competitiveness.

Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development highlighted India Post’s substantial growth potential and stressed the importance of workforce empowerment, accountability and improved service delivery. He called for standardized procedures and real-time monitoring to address parcel delivery delays and enhance customer satisfaction.

The Ministers directed Postal Circles to sustain growth momentum during the festive and peak parcel season, strengthen Parcels and International Relations & Global Business, accelerate the onboarding of Citizen-Centric Services in collaboration with State Governments, and maintain expenditure discipline. The review also emphasized a cluster-based approach focusing on Agro-Logistics and International Business; MSMEs, ODOP and Tourism; and Citizen-Centric Services, Financial Inclusion, Insurance and Rural Logistics. Guided by the spirit of Jan Seva, the Department will leverage its extensive network and workforce to unlock new business opportunities, enhance operational efficiency and advance towards financial sustainability.

A historic Q2 for @IndiaPostOffice, after a historic Q1. Growth momentum continues, with Q2 revenue at ₹4,202 crore, up 25% year on year, led by: Parcel: +71% PLI/RPLI: +44% IR & GB: +38% Chaired the Quarterly Business Review with all 23 circles, where 19 crossed 80% of their Q2 targets. Reaffirmed our commitment to working as one India Post family, with greater synergy and a unified focus on scaling up and serving our customers to the best of our ability. #DakSewaJanSewa

headline: FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON ARRIVES IN MALDIVES
paras: Ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS) – INS Tir, INS Sujata and Indian Coast Guard Ship Sarathi – arrived off Malé, Maldives, on 21 Oct 2026 as part of the Squadron’s Long Range Training Deployment. The Squadron received a warm welcome from the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF), reflecting the strong maritime partnership and close regional ties between the two nations.

During the port call, the Senior Officer, First Training Squadron, called on the Chief of Defence Force, MNDF, and the Commandant, MNDF Coast Guard. Discussions focused on sustained engagement and multifaceted maritime collaboration between the Indian Navy and MNDF. The Senior Officer 1TS also called on Shri G Balasubramaniam, High Commissioner of India to the Maldives. As part of the training exchanges, trainees of 1TS visited the Girifushi Training Centre.
Cross-deck visits, sports fixtures, social interactions and outreach activities are also planned during the visit to foster camaraderie and mutual understanding between the two forces.

The ongoing visit reaffirms enhanced interoperability between the Indian Navy and MNDF, and underscores the growing maritime cooperation between the two nations, in line with the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

headline: Defence Secretary inaugurates Hindi Library ‘GYANDEEP’ at Sena Bhawan in New Delhi under Special Campaign 6
paras: Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh inaugurated the newly established Hindi library, ‘GYANDEEP’, in Sena Bhawan, New Delhi on October 22, 2026 as part of Special Campaign 6, being conducted by the Ministry of Defence from October 02 - 31, 2026. The initiative aims to promote Hindi books and literature, encourage the use of Hindi in official work, and strengthen the culture of working in Hindi in pursuit of excellence in the implementation of Rajbhasha.

As part of the campaign, approximately 35,000 square feet of space has been freed up in South Block through cleaning and disposal of old records and surrendered to the Project Yuga Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM). 1,361 e-files have been closed and 1,746 physical files have been weeded out. The disposal of e-waste and other obsolete items has generated revenue amounting to ₹4.22 lakh.
On the occasion, the Defence Secretary also felicitated eight Swachhta Veers in recognition of their special contributions during the ongoing campaign.

Maintenance and cleaning of offices, segregation and disposal of e-waste, and related activities are also being carried out regularly across various offices and buildings of the Ministry of Defence, including Sena Bhawan, Kartavya Bhawan-II, Vayu Bhawan and KG Marg.

headline: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 to be organised from Nov 28 to Dec 12, 2026, on the theme “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”
subhead: Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, launches Registration Portal for KTS 5.0
paras: Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today launched the registration portal for the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS 5.0) scheduled to be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026. The programme will celebrate, reaffirm and strengthen the age-old civilizational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning, strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.

Speaking at the Launch, Shri Pralhad Joshi said that since ancient times, the country has had a strong cultural unity. He noted that many people visited Kashi and Rameswaram as part of their religious traditions, reflecting the deep-rooted cultural bonds between the northern and southern parts of India. He stated that the Programme would bring together students, teachers, writers, professionals, agriculturalists, artists, women and spiritual scholars. He also highlighted that educational outreach initiatives would be carried out in higher education institutions to familiarise students with the objectives of Kashi Tamil Sangamam. The Union Minister reiterated that Kashi Tamil Sangamam played an important role in strengthening national unity and celebrating India’s shared civilisational heritage.

The first Kashi Tamil Sangamam was held in 2022 and over the last four editions, it facilitated meaningful exchanges of knowledge, language, traditions and lived experiences between the two regions. The Event is organized by the Department of Higher Education, Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras; Banaras Hindu University (BHU); Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Chennai; Uttar Pradesh Government and Central Govt Departments/Ministries of Culture, Railways, School Education, Tourism, Textiles, Food Processing Industries, Information & Broadcasting, Skill Development & Entrepreneurship, etc.
Theme for 2026: “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”

The theme of KTS 5.0 is “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”. The fifth edition seeks to bring the timeless ethical and moral wisdom of the classical Tamil text Thirukkural closer to the youth and learners across the country. Through educational engagement, multilingual resources and wider public outreach, the programme seeks to encourage reading, understanding and application of universal values as enshrined in the text, in everyday life.
Participation and Itinerary

As part of the Programme, around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, organized into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey comprising four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary will include Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, featuring cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements. The emphasis on youth participation will enable a new generation to engage meaningfully with India’s classical knowledge traditions and carry their values into contemporary academic, professional and social life.
Registration Details

Interested applicants may register through the official portal at https://kashitamil.iitm.ac.in/ hosted by IIT Madras with effect from October 22, 2026. The Portal will accept applications till November 13, 2026 under seven categories: (i) Students, (ii) Teachers, (iii) Writers and Media Professionals, (iv) Agriculture and Allied Sectors, (v) Professionals and Artisans, (vi) Women and (vii) Spiritual leaders.
Major Initiatives under KTS 5.0

The Ministry of Education invites eligible applicants from Tamil Nadu, especially youth and students, to register for Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 and participate in this celebration of India’s cultural oneness, linguistic diversity and shared civilisational inheritance.

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
headline: CAQM Reviews Air Pollution Control Measures in Punjab and Haryana, Calls for Prompt Ground-Level Action
subhead: Focus on prevention of Paddy Stubble Burning, effective utilization of CRM Machinery, stronger Enforcement and control of other key Pollution Sources
paras: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, held separate review meetings with the Governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh today to review the measures being undertaken for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning and abatement of other key sources of air pollution, calling for prompt action(s) on the ground.

The meeting with the Government of Punjab focused on implementation of the State Action Plan for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning in accordance with CAQM Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026. The Commission reviewed on-ground enforcement measures, District-level preparedness and monitoring mechanisms in place for effective paddy stubble management.

The availability, deployment and effective utilization of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery at the District and farmer levels were reviewed, along with the identification of gaps in machinery utilization and arrangements for the collection, transportation and utilization of paddy straw through in-situ and ex-situ management. The Commission emphasized the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure effective utilization of available machinery during the peak harvesting period.

The meeting also covered field validation of burnt-area assessment through satellite-based fire alerts, along with District-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring stubble-burning incidents. Compliance with CAQM Direction No. 92, mandating the use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns, and progress towards prescribed targets for biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also reviewed.

The meeting with the Government of Haryana covered a broader range of air pollution sources, including paddy stubble burning, abatement of vehicular pollution, dust from roads and open areas, dust from construction and demolition (C&D) activities and industrial pollution, along with other identified sectoral measures.

With regard to paddy stubble burning, the Commission reviewed implementation of the State Action Plan, including on-ground enforcement, deployment and utilization of CRM machinery, crop-residue supply-chain management, field validation of burnt-area assessment and the use of drones and low-cost sensors for monitoring burning incidents. Compliance with Direction No. 92 regarding biomass pellets/ briquettes in brick kilns and progress on biomass co-firing in thermal power plants were also taken up.

The review of vehicular pollution covered installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system at fuel and CNG stations for enforcement of requirements relating to valid Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs), action against end-of-life vehicles, adoption of cleaner mobility measures and progress towards phasing out diesel-operated auto rickshaws in NCR Districts.

Measures for dust mitigation from roads and open areas, including road-dust control and mechanized road sweeping, were also reviewed. The Commission further examined measures for controlling dust emissions from C&D activities and implementation of prescribed dust-mitigation measures. The review also covered industrial pollution control, including compliance with applicable norms and monitoring and enforcement measures relating to industrial units and other identified sources.

The Commission emphasized the need for time-bound implementation of State Action Plans, its enforcement and continuous field-level monitoring, supported by close coordination among the concerned State Departments, District Administrations and enforcement agencies. The States were advised to address implementation gaps on priority and ensure timely corrective action across the respective sectors. The Commission emphasized on greater facilitation of farmers with in-situ crop residue management machinery and strengthened ex-situ mechanism. State Governments of Haryana and Punjab were also advised to implement IEC Action Plans on-ground more effectively.

The Commission emphasized that paddy stubble management should be pursued not merely as a measure to prevent burning, but as an opportunity to improve the well-being of citizens while fostering a robust industrial ecosystem of a circular economy, with greater utilization of paddy straw as a resource. The Commission called for prompt action at the ground level and further cautioned the District Administrations that any laxity that leads to rise in stubble-burning incidents shall be viewed seriously.

CAQM reiterated that sustained and coordinated efforts by the State Governments and all concerned agencies are essential for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning and comprehensive abatement of air pollution, particularly during the critical winter period.

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
headline: At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
subhead: Government translating Policy Intent into Meaningful Action through Clear Policies and Regulatory Reforms: Shri Bhupender Yadav
paras: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today addressed the Circular Economy Conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in New Delhi. He highlighted India’s efforts to translate policy intent into meaningful action through clear policies, regulatory reforms, digital compliance systems and a whole-of-government approach to advance the circular economy.

Congratulations to Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan and Krishna Nagar on winning the Bronze Medal in the Mixed Doubles SH6 Para Badminton event at the Asian Para Games 2026! Their dedication has brought another proud moment for Indian Para Badminton. Wishing them continued success in the competitions ahead: PM @narendramodi

In his address, Shri Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Government had progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams: plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste. These rules focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. The Minister also highlighted that as on date, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.

Highlighting the role of EPR, the Minister said that the framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life. The transfer of EPR certificates provided financial incentives to recyclers, encouraging capacity expansion, technological advancement and increased recycling, while contributing to job creation and livelihoods across the recycling value chain. Shri Yadav emphasised that regulation alone could not create a circular economy and highlighted the importance of Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, which calls for mindful and deliberate resource utilisation instead of destructive consumption.

On Industry concerns regarding digital compliance, EPR market operations and transaction timelines, Shri Yadav invited stakeholders to continue sharing practical problems and suggestions. He said the Government is working on a market-based approach and urged industry representatives to engage openly to resolve outstanding issues. On plastic waste management, the Minister called for greater coordination between producers and recyclers to address concerns over the availability of recyclable material and recycling capacity. He said the objective went beyond issuing certificates to creating jobs, strengthening local industry capacity, promoting knowledge-sharing and advancing technology.

While talking about Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, Shri Yadav stressed the need for technology adoption, capacity building, online monitoring, stronger accountability and financial sustainability of urban local bodies. The Minister also highlighted the importance of four-stream segregation of solid waste – wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste – and public participation. Shri Yadav concluded by emphasising that effective implementation of the SWM Rules would help control legacy waste and strengthen urban systems. He called for coordinated efforts by the government, industry and urban local bodies to advance the circular economy. He further called for stronger recovery of critical minerals from e-waste and batteries, and greater industry participation in developing secondary raw-material markets and strengthening supply-chain traceability.

headline: CBDT actively implements Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and administrative efficiency
paras: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is actively executing Special Campaign 6 for Swachhata, focused on enhancing cleanliness in government offices and resolving pending matters including public grievances and MP/PMO/State Govt references. In accordance with DARPG guidelines, the campaign is being enthusiastically implemented by field formations nationwide.

The campaign commenced with a Preparatory Phase (September 15-30, 2026) to identify key targets, followed by the Implementation Phase (October 2 - 31, 2026). Income Tax offices across the country have shown strong participation, with ongoing efforts aimed at boosting workplace efficiency, fostering sustainability, and ensuring timely resolution of grievances.
In the first two weeks of the Implementation Phase, the campaign has already delivered notable results:

These results underscore the Department's firm commitment to embedding cleanliness practices, enhancing record management, and advancing digitization and responsible e-waste disposal. The CBDT Nodal Officer is working in close coordination with regional counterparts to ensure effective implementation, with daily progress updates being uploaded to the SCDPM portal managed by DARPG.

To enhance public engagement, CBDT has made more than 150 posts on X (formerly Twitter), highlighting achievements, best practices, and citizen-centric efforts. The campaign is being widely promoted across digital platforms, reinforcing the Department's focus on transparency, participation and good governance.
During the campaign, the department has taken many initiatives and some of these are:
A. Citizen Centric Initiatives by Income Tax Department in West Bengal & Sikkim as well as Gujarat Regions

As part of Special Campaign 6, the Income Tax Department, West Bengal & Sikkim and Gujarat, carried out a cleanliness drive at St. John’s Church, a renowned tourist spot in Kolkata; Kamudini Homes Higher Secondary School, Kalimpong; Municipal Girls High School, Darjeeling; pilgrim place, Mehsana; Vastrapur Railway Station, Ahmedabad etc. in addition to Income Tax Offices at Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad. The initiative reinforced the Department's commitment to cleanliness and sustainability.

The office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal & Sikkim organised a ‘Waste to Art’ exhibition from 01.10.2026 to 06.10.2026 at Oikotaan Rooftop, Aayakar Bhawan Annexe, Kolkata featuring innovative artworks made from discarded household materials. Used plastic bottles, cans, containers and other scrap materials were transformed into striking depictions of human figures, animal replicas, planters and decorative artefacts alongside a photography gallery. The initiative beautifully blended artistic creativity with environmental consciousness, promoting the message of waste-to-wealth and sustainable living.
C. Space Optimisation and Office Beautification at Delhi

The Office of the Director General of Income Tax (Investigation), Delhi converted an under-utilised floor area into a ‘Laghu Pustakalaya’, a mini library with a reading lounge, book cabinets, suitable lighting, seating and indoor plants. The initiative promotes optimal space utilisation and provides a conducive environment for reading and staff well-being.
D. E-Waste Management

As part of Special Campaign 6, the Income Tax Offices at Kolkata, Chennai and Bhubaneswar undertook initiatives for the proper disposal of e-waste generated in office premises, promoting environmentally responsible waste management and ensuring the systematic handling of discarded electronic items.
E waste Collection [ Aayakar Bhawan, Chennai and Bhubaneshwar]
D. Cleanliness Drive and Green Initiative at Aayakar Bhawan Dakshin, Kolkata

The Office of the Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-2, Kolkata restored an overgrown garden through clearance and beautification, incorporating fountain features, decorative lamp pillars and potted plants to create a well-maintained green space for officers, staff and visitors. The initiative promoted a greener workplace and reinforced the Departments’ commitment to cleanliness and sustainability.

The Income Tax Department also actively participated in the 'Swachhata Hi Seva' (SHS) campaign during the month of September 2026. Key initiatives included the Swachhata pledge, Sustainable Waste Management, medical camps for Safai Mitras, cleaning up of parks and other public spaces, engaging and sensitizing school students and youth for Swachhata through 'Swachhata Gyan Yatra' and also actively participating in the nationwide Shramdaan - 'Ek Din Ek Ghanta Ek Saath'.

The initiatives undertaken by CBDT under Special Campaign 6 reaffirm its commitment to Swachhata, efficiency, and citizen-centric governance. Through innovation, active participation, and sustainable practices, the Department continues to drive the vision of a clean, efficient, and technology-enabled administration, ensuring that the spirit of Swachhata remains a year-round pursuit across all field formations.

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
headline: Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to Focus on Investment, Value Addition and Export Opportunities in Inland Fisheries
paras: The Department of Fisheries, Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India (GoI) are organising Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026 to be held on 23 October 2026 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The Conclave aims to strengthen linkages between inland fisheries production and investment, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition and export markets. It seeks to encourage a shift from a predominantly production-oriented approach towards an integrated value-chain model, with a focus on improving market access and returns for fishermen and fish farmers.

The Conclave will bring together investors, exporters, fishers, more than 1,000 fish farmers from various parts of Madhya Pradesh, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), entrepreneurs, start-ups, processors, financial institutions, research organisations and other stakeholders. Deliberations will focus on enterprise development, access to finance, market linkages and opportunities for collaboration across the inland fisheries value chain, with particular emphasis on integrating inland States into the fisheries investment and export ecosystem.

A key feature of the Conclave will be the release of the MADHYA PRADESH FISHERIES INVESTMENT AND EXPORT GUIDELINES, 2026. Madhya Pradesh has been notified by the Center as a Reservoir Fisheries Cluster. The policy is intended to facilitate investment across key segments of the fisheries value chain, including hatcheries, fish seed and feed, reservoir and cage fisheries, aquatic animal health, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, logistics, value addition and market development.

The programme will also feature the release of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) on the export potential of inland States, the virtual inauguration of Integrated Cage Culture Units. During the event, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj will hand over the Administrative Approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in Madhya Pradesh. These initiatives are expected to support investment in inland fisheries, promote the productive utilisation of water resources and encourage enterprise development.

The Conclave assumes significance in the context of India's expanding fisheries sector and its growing contribution to food security, livelihoods and export earnings. India’s fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25, of which 151.60 lakh tonnes came from inland fisheries, accounting for nearly three-fourths of the country's total fish production. India's seafood exports were valued at ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26. These figures highlight the importance of strengthening infrastructure, processing capabilities and market linkages to realise the potential of inland fisheries.

Madhya Pradesh, with nearly 4.50 lakh hectares of water area, offers considerable potential for inland fisheries development. The Conclave seeks to connect the State's production base, along with that of other inland States, with investment, processing, value addition and domestic and export markets.

The Conclave will be graced by Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; and Shri Narayan Singh Pawar, Hon’ble Minister, Department of Fisherman Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh.

Through stakeholder engagement and deliberations on investment and market development, the Conclave seeks to promote more competitive and market-oriented inland fisheries value chains, expand opportunities for enterprises and exporters, and strengthen livelihood and income opportunities for fishermen and fish farmers.
